text.p: Indonesia's largest cement maker PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa said on Friday its current large expansion programme would have no negative impact and only benefit shareholders.

"We have the money...we need to expand. This is in our shareholders interests," president director Sudwikatmono told reporters after a ceremony marking the foundation of its 11th plant in Bogor, West Java.
He was replying to questions that the firm's large capacity expansion programme and plan to buy its subsidiary Indofood's rights issue may have a negative impact on its 1997 earnings.

Sudwikatmono said cement supply was expected to lag behind demand in the near future as the goverment had given about 43 permits to companies to build cement plants, but less than five had constructed their factories.
Separately, he said the firm's plan to spend 650 billion rupiah to buy part of the Indofood rights issue this year was not expected to have negative impacts on its 1997 earnings.
Sudwikatmono declined to comment further on the two matters.
Indocement had said it expects to buy part of Indofood's rights issue scheduled later this year to maintain its 52-percent stake in its food subsidiary.
Indofood had said it planned to acquire six companies from the Salim Group with interests in plantations, distribution as well as cooking oils and fats through its rights issue and loans.
Both Indocement and Indofood are parts of Indonesia's largest conglomerate the Salim Group. The acquisition was expected to cost about 1.750 trillion rupiah.
Sudwikatmono said Indocement's current expansion programme includes building new plants in Kalimantan as well as Cirebon and Citereup, both in West Java.
